newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power sees earnings growth in new fields.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power sees earnings growth in new fields.

text.p: Singapore Power chief Ho Kwon Ping said on Wednesday that diversification into sectors like telecommunications will provide additional sources of earnings before the state company loses monopoly in two years.
"If our bid for the telecom licence is successful, the new business will provide an additional source of earnings growth for Singapore Power in the future," Ho told Reuters in an interview.

Singapore Power (SP), state-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia, British Telecom and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp 95432.T have formed a consortium to bid for a basic telecommunication services license in Singapore.
Ho said the pursuit of a licence, due to become effective in April 2000, was the company's biggest diversification effort and that he was confident the consortium would put in a strong bid.

"The telecommunication business is synergistic to our core business of electricity generation, transmission and distribution. We will be leveraging off our existing assets in venturing into telecommunication," Ho said.

"We will make use of its extensive underground cable network and some 7,000 substations across the island to offer a full range multi media services as well as the basic telephone services for which we are bidding for a license to operate," Ho added.
The Singapore government has said it will allow at least one and possibly two new operators to operate fixed line services to compete with domestic monopoly Singapore Telecom.
Singapore Power's decision to diversify followed the government's announcement of plans to open up the power industry to the private sector in about two years.
"Everything that we are doing now is preparing for competition," Ho said when asked how Singapore Power planned to cope with competition once it loses its power monopoly.
"One would be in terms of our existing core business, how to gear that ready for competition and the other one would be how do we look for new businesses."

He said the company aimed to meet competition in its core business of power generation and distribution through productivity gains, increased efficiency, better customer service and "squeezing the most out of its existing assests".
Ho said it aimed to generate between Singapore $300-500 million (US$200-350 million) in cost savings through productivity improvement measures over the next 10 years.
He also said that, through wholly-owned subsidiary Singapore Power International, it will set aside about S$1.0 billion for overseas investment over the next five years.
It was looking into opportunities in China, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, India and Australia, he said.
Ho said SP's diversifications and improving on its core business would have an impact on the bottom line, but declined to provide figures.
SP was scheduled to be listed in mid-1996, but the government has delayed the move indefinitely.
